item.title: Tourist jailed over airport bomb remark claims unlawful detention
item.description: A Croatian tourist detained for a week over a flippant remark at Malta International Airport has filed a habeas corpus application claiming unlawful detention. Blazenko Djuran, 61, said he wished to plead guilty when arraigned, but Magistrate Abigail Critien entered a not-guilty plea, saying she would not accept a guilty plea from someone who did not know what he was charged with. The incident began when staff told him his bag was too bulky for his Ryanair flight, to which he replied that it was not like there was a bomb in it; he was charged with spreading false news likely to alarm the public. His lawyers José Herrera, Martina Herrera and Matthew Xuereb argue he had every right to admit the charges at his arraignment.

item.title: Abela thanks Lagarde as ECB president announces 2027 exit
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela paid tribute to Christine Lagarde after she announced she will step down as President of the European Central Bank on 7 February 2027, several months before her term was due to end. Abela wrote on X that he appreciated her leadership and commitment to safeguarding stability during exceptionally challenging times for Europe. Lagarde has led the ECB since November 2019, overseeing the pandemic and a period of soaring inflation, with her rate decisions having had a direct impact on Maltese households and businesses.

item.title: Xjenza Malta showcases over 50 publicly funded research projects
item.description: Xjenza Malta opened the third edition of its annual Research and Innovation Days on Thursday, bringing together researchers, students, academics and industry for a two-day event on the impact of publicly funded research in Malta. The R EXPO presented 12 projects with working prototypes, including displays open to schoolchildren, while more than 40 completed projects were presented by video, tracing work from fundamental studies to applied research and prototype development. CEO Silvio Scerri said the projects demonstrate the value of investing in research at every stage.

item.title: Clubclass sets up €250,000 student service continuity fund
item.description: Malta-based English language school Clubclass said it will establish a €250,000 Service Continuity Trust Fund to support students and education partners if the school is unable to deliver prepaid services. The family-owned firm, founded in 1999, said the money would come from retained earnings and be ring-fenced from ordinary operating funds, following closures elsewhere in the international language education sector. The fund is intended to help eligible students continue their studies and maintain accommodation in Malta, is expected to become operational on 1 January 2027, and will carry no additional fee for students or agents.

item.title: Maltese-flagged yachts can now apply for US cruising licences
item.description: Maltese-flagged pleasure yachts can now apply for US cruising licences, according to Minister for Sustainable Mobility Chris Bonnett. Malta was formally added to the list of countries eligible for cruising privileges under 19 CFR 4.94(b) following diplomatic engagement with the United States, with the decision published in the US Federal Register on 29 October. Bonnett said the change removes a longstanding competitive disadvantage in one of the worlds main yachting markets and introduces a commercial advantage to registering a private yacht under the Malta flag. Licensed yachts stand to benefit from exemptions from certain customs entry and clearance procedures, manifest requirements, permits to proceed and tonnage duties.

item.title: Constitutional Court upholds five-year minimum sentence for sex with minors
item.description: The Constitutional Court dismissed Adrian Piscopo's challenge to the mandatory five-year minimum prison sentence for sexual activity with a person under 16, ruling the statutory minimum does not amount to inhuman or degrading punishment under Article 3 of the European Convention on Human Rights. The court, presided over by Chief Justice Mark Chetcuti, also rejected the argument that proceedings should not continue if the alleged victim no longer wishes to pursue the case. Judges described the appeal as frivolous and vexatious, ordering Piscopo to pay €2,500 in costs.

item.title: Swieqi confrontation: contractor says man was a neighbour, not a worker
item.description: A construction company linked to a confrontation in Swieqi has said the man seen throwing an object towards a woman filming the incident was a neighbour who entered the site without authorisation, not one of its workers. The footage, shared by Swieqi Deputy Mayor Jordan Galea Pace, showed the man shouting and apparently throwing an object during an argument with workers; it remains unclear what the object was. A.Aquilina Building Contractors Ltd said it does not condone or tolerate aggressive or threatening behaviour. Galea Pace condemned what he described as intimidation towards the resident and her daughter, including comments allegedly directed at the woman because of her gender, and said residents have a right to feel safe in their locality.

item.title: First Malta study on men who pay for sex finds a third did so in adolescence
item.description: A first-of-its-kind study in Malta found that a third of the men surveyed had paid for sex in adolescence. Dr Yanika Borg presented the research, The Cost of Buying Sex, at a conference organised by Dar Hosea on Friday, drawing on interviews with 72 men about their attitudes, motivations and views of the practice. The study links the behaviour to a sense of dominance, the objectification of women and exploitation, and notes that such cases are rarely reported to the authorities.

item.title: Short-let operator says €10 tourist tax triggered four cancellations in two days
item.description: A Maltese short-let operator said he received four booking cancellations in two days after the government announced the tourist eco-contribution would rise from €1.50 to €10 per person per night. André Grech told Lovin Malta the cancellations involved families planning holidays in the quieter shoulder months rather than groups of young people, and that losing them costs other local businesses as well. He noted that four adults staying seven nights would face €280 in eco-tax alone, excluding flights and accommodation, and called the sudden cancellations highly unusual for his business.

item.title: Curia staff deal is first in Malta with dedicated mental health fund
item.description: The Curia of the Archbishop and the Malta General Workers Union have concluded a new collective agreement for Curia and ecclesiastical court employees covering 2026-2030. Around 140 staff stand to benefit, and the agreement is the first in Malta to include a dedicated mental health fund, allowing employees to use professional mental health services with the cost covered under their own names. It also provides wage improvements, better allowances, greater flexibility in working hours and the possibility of remote work, alongside enhanced training and professional development. The deal was signed on behalf of the Curia by Administrative Secretary Michael Pace Ross and for the union by Deputy General Secretary Isabelle Farrugia.

item.title: Missing man found in Gżira after public appeal from mother
item.description: A man with Down Syndrome who went missing after being dropped off at a closed day centre in Baħar iċ-Ċagħaq was found safe and well in the Gżira area on Friday. His mother, Lorraine Hussain, appealed for help after Malik, 31, failed to arrive at the Aġenzija Sapport centre as expected, and Inclusion Minister Julia Farrugia also issued a public appeal. A neighbour had dropped Malik off at the centre in the morning by mistake, and he later tried to walk home. Farrugia confirmed he was found and thanked parents who called with information.

item.title: Employer bodies say Budget 2027 TCN measures lack careful calibration
item.description: Maltas main employer bodies said on Friday that Budget 2027s measures on third-country nationals and business costs fall short of the careful planning they say economic transformation requires. The Malta Chamber of Commerce, the Malta Hotels and Restaurants Association, the Malta Chamber of SMEs and the Malta Employers Association said the TCN measures were announced without prior stakeholder consultation or a comprehensive socio-economic impact assessment. They warned that higher permitting, public transport and childcare charges could fuel inflation and undermine business continuity, saying the package gives the impression of a government urgently seeking fresh revenue to honour electoral commitments. The groups said they would back incentives for digitalisation, automation and workforce upskilling, but could not support rushed policy decisions introduced overnight.

item.title: Prosecution closes case in Lassane Cisse murder trial
item.description: Prosecutor Abigail Caruana Vella asked the jury to hold Lorin Scicluna responsible for the murder of Lassane Cisse when she resumed her closing address on Friday. She argued that Scicluna cannot escape responsibility simply by claiming his co-accused Francesco Fenech fired the fatal shots, and questioned unexplained gaps in CCTV footage showing the movements of the vehicle and the victim. The two men are being tried separately, a choice the prosecution acknowledged would have made a single trial easier.

item.title: Man cleared of 2015 Paceville stampede handed suspended sentence on appeal
item.description: The Court of Appeal has overturned the acquittal of a man cleared over the 2015 Paceville stampede and handed him a suspended sentence and a fine. Zach Latif had been cleared by the Magistrates Court of negligently causing grievous injuries, carrying a weapon at an entertainment venue, breaching public order and possessing pepper spray, after releasing spray inside the packed Plus One club caused panicked crowds to break a staircase handrail. Presiding Madame Justice Edwina Grima ruled that a sworn 2015 statement in which Latif admitted buying and discharging a 40ml pepper spray canister should have been used as evidence, and rejected his claims that he was acting in self-defence or as a good Samaritan. The Attorney General had appealed the acquittal.

item.title: Witness tells court Valletta assault accused was "a great kid"
item.description: A witness told a court that James Manfre, 32, behaved out of character when he allegedly assaulted police officers during a disturbance in St Mark Street, Valletta on 30 September. John Pierre Farrugia, who has known the accused since he was a baby, described him as "a great kid" while testifying before Magistrate Giannella Camilleri Busuttil. Manfre denies 16 charges including assaulting and injuring police officers, damaging public property, resisting arrest and breaching bail conditions.

item.title: Central Government debt hits nearly €12bn at end of Q3
item.description: Central Government debt stood at €11,956.6 million at the end of September 2026, up €846.4 million on the same point in 2025, the National Statistics Office said. The rise was driven mainly by Malta Government Stocks, up €658.9 million, and by Treasury Bills, with euro coins issued in the name of the Treasury also higher. The Consolidated Fund reported a deficit of €484.8 million, while recurrent revenue rose €704.2 million and total expenditure rose €935.8 million over the first nine months.

item.title: Paola mayors bank freeze order withdrawn, PM says
item.description: Prime Minister Robert Abela says the garnishee order freezing Paola mayor Jason Silvios personal bank account has been withdrawn, after the State Advocate intervened on the councillors behalf. The order was sought by a developer after the Paola Local Council appealed a Planning Authority permit for a multi-storey block on Triq Ninu Cremona, which the council says would damage the towns urban conservation area. Councillors had walked out of a council meeting in solidarity with the mayor, and the government said it will protect public officials who challenge planning decisions.

item.title: Finance Minister: TCNs will not disappear after Budget 2027 measures
item.description: Finance Minister Clyde Caruana has said third-country nationals will not disappear from Malta after the Budget 2027 measures, which he said would mainly affect demand for future TCNs rather than those already living and working in the country. Speaking on TVMs XTRA opposite PN finance spokesperson Adrian Delia, he said the measures are designed to act on wages and prices and are a step towards controlling population growth, warning Malta could reach 800,000 people by 2040 if the current rate does not change. The measures have drawn criticism from unions, NGOs and employers, with the General Workers Union calling them purely populist.

item.title: Bill to reform Malta Enterprise and INDIS Malta due within days
item.description: Economy Minister Silvio Schembri says a bill strengthening the operational framework of Malta Enterprise and INDIS Malta will be presented in parliament in the coming days, alongside a first national industrial policy. More than 100 million is earmarked for digitalisation next year, with a separate 120 million scheme due to start by year-end offering a 60% tax credit on eligible automation, AI and digitalisation investment. An updated national AI strategy running to 2030, with more than 80 measures, is due to be launched next month.

item.title: Dalli urges EU energy flexibility for Maltese households
item.description: Energy Minister Miriam Dalli told an EU Energy Council in Luxembourg that member states need the flexibility to take measures suited to their own circumstances, even where the EU acts collectively on energy security. She said Maltas priority is keeping energy tariffs affordable for families and businesses while strengthening national energy infrastructure, including cross-border links to networks beyond EU borders.

item.title: Man granted bail over Mercury Towers knife incident
item.description: Martin John Azzopardi was granted bail after he allegedly entered Mercury Towers in St Julians on 27 October carrying a steak knife and making his way to the offices used by developer Joseph Portelli and his family. The court heard he left the knife wrapped in a napkin in a bathroom before the meeting, and that it was found by an employee after he had left. Magistrate Gabriella Vella granted conditional bail with a personal guarantee, a three-year protection order, restrictions on entering certain locations and electronic monitoring. Azzopardi pleaded not guilty and is presumed innocent.

item.title: 15% of Maltese firms use AI in hiring and firing decisions
item.description: A Eurobarometer survey finds around 15% of Maltese companies use AI to assist with hiring, promotion and dismissal decisions, well above the EU average of 9% and among the highest rates in the EU. Overall, 41% of Maltese SMEs and mid-caps engage with workplace AI, roughly in line with the EU average, and human oversight remains the norm only 2% of businesses report fully automated decisions.

item.title: Nurses union: 95% of private elderly home staff are TCNs
item.description: Paul Pace, president of the nurses and midwives union, said 95% or more of staff in Maltas private elderly homes are third-country nationals, with the share also high in public hospitals 40% at Mater Dei and 60% at San Vincent de Paul. Speaking on Newsbooks Attwalit, he said those workers have already paid their share for years and hoped the new Budget fees on TCNs would not drive them out of the health sector.

item.title: Government and PN clash over Budget measures and nationality
item.description: Government deputy minister Ramona Attard and Nationalist Party finance spokesman Mark Anthony Sammut clashed over the Budgets measures on third-country nationals. Attard said the government does not distinguish between nationalities and that people already settled in Malta with residence permits will not be affected, while those still arriving will be expected to contribute through childcare and public transport costs. Sammut said the party would not make it unviable for people to keep working in Malta.

item.title: Malta Boat Show returns to Cottonera with 150 boats
item.description: The third edition of the Malta Boat Show opened at Dockyard Creek in Cottonera, running to 1 November with around 150 boats and yachts, some 70 exhibitors and about 1.5km of quays. International boatbuilders are taking part for the first time and the event includes the new Malta Wake Show. item.title: One in seven Maltese firms use AI to hire, promote or dismiss staff
item.description: One in seven Maltese businesses uses or plans to use artificial intelligence in decisions affecting employees, a Eurobarometer survey found. Around 15 per cent of Maltese SMEs and mid-caps deploy AI in human resources decisions, well above the EU average of 9 per cent, while 12 per cent use it for recruitment and candidate screening. Overall workplace AI use stands at 41 per cent, close to the EU average, and human oversight remains the norm, with only 2 per cent of businesses allowing fully automated decisions.

item.title: Malta elected co-facilitator for UN convention on older persons
item.description: Malta has been elected co-facilitator for the drafting of a United Nations convention on the rights of older persons, Foreign Affairs Minister Chris Fearne announced. Malta will work alongside Lesotho on the treaty's implementation and review mechanisms as the UN Intergovernmental Working Group on the Human Rights of Older Persons concludes its second session in Geneva. The proposed convention aims to establish a legally binding framework protecting older persons from discrimination, abuse and neglect.

item.title: Ten primary schools to get air conditioning under €6m programme
item.description: Education Minister Byron Camilleri said ten primary schools will be fitted with air conditioning under a €6 million programme, with installation targeted over the next scholastic year. The schools named are Baħrija, Pembroke, Luqa, Mġarr, Xgħajra, Gudja, Għargħur, Żebbuġ, Naxxar and Qormi, and 30 schools already have systems installed. Speaking at a Budget 2027 conference, Camilleri said Malta's PISA results were unsatisfactory and that the measures aim to address the country's reading culture.

item.title: Shop ceiling collapses in Valletta; man inside escapes uninjured
item.description: Part of the ceiling of a shop in South Street, Valletta collapsed on Friday morning while a man was inside. Police and the Occupational Health and Safety Authority attended after officers were alerted at 10.20am; the man was uninjured and declined an ambulance, with a medical team also on site. The street was closed while authorities assessed the building.

item.title: Paceville glass attacker has five-year jail term suspended
item.description: A man originally sentenced to five years in prison for smashing a glass into another man's head at Bar Native in Paceville in October 2020 has had his jail term converted to a suspended sentence. The court found there was insufficient proof that the assault caused the victim serious and permanent disfigurement, which changed the legal classification of the injury. His five-year term became two years, suspended for four years.

item.title: More tourists, but spending per head falls in first nine months
item.description: Inbound tourists for the first nine months of 2026 reached 3,599,493, up 17.0 per cent on the same period of 2025, the National Statistics Office said. Total tourist expenditure rose 13.9 per cent to €3,450.5 million and nights spent increased 9.6 per cent to 21.5 million. Spending per capita nevertheless fell to €959 from €985, with British, Italian and Polish residents accounting for 47.4 per cent of arrivals.

item.title: Over a third of Maltese young adults still live with their parents
item.description: More than one in three young adults in Malta are still living with their parents, according to new Eurostat figures. Data for 2025 shows 37.1 per cent of people aged between 25 and 34 remained in the parental home, seven percentage points above the EU average of 30.1 per cent, ranking Malta 12th of the EU's 27 member states. Croatia recorded the highest share at 62.3 per cent, while Denmark was lowest at 3.9 per cent.

item.title: Four acquitted over 2015 Paqpaqli crash
item.description: Four men were acquitted of all criminal charges over the 2015 Paqpaqli għall-Istrina crash that injured dozens of spectators at Malta International Airport. Prosecutors failed to prove that the defendants, the last individuals facing proceedings over the incident, were personally responsible for public safety at the charity motoring event, though the court acknowledged serious shortcomings in how it was organised. About 26 people were injured, some critically, when a Porsche 918 Spyder crashed into the crowd.

item.title: Paola mayor's bank freeze order withdrawn after PM's pledge
item.description: Paola Mayor Jason Silvio has had the garnishee order against him withdrawn, following controversy over a developer's decision to target him personally amid a planning dispute. Prime Minister Robert Abela said he had been informed that the order was withdrawn, adding that the mayor can continue his work with greater peace of mind. The freeze followed a Paola Local Council appeal against a Planning Authority decision on a development in Triq Ninu Cremona, and came after the State Advocate intervened.

item.title: Free Maltese lessons for foreign residents under Budget measures
item.description: Free Maltese language lessons for foreign residents are being offered as part of the new Budget 2027 measures, in a move intended to ease integration. Kay Lee Micallef, who does not live in Malta, proposed the initiative, which will run two classes of about 15 people each, weekly, over four or five months. The lessons will teach Maltese as a foreign language without leading to a certificate, focusing instead on learning and practice.

item.title: Xjenza Malta and ESA open fifth call for space research projects
item.description: Xjenza Malta and the European Space Agency have opened the fifth call for proposals under the European Cooperative Programme for Space Research and Industry, with the call opening on 2 November. Maltese companies, researchers and research organisations will be able to apply for funding to turn research into space-related innovation. The agency held an information session on 13 October covering how to prepare competitive proposals and avoid common application errors.

item.title: AFM gives no answer on 30 people allegedly pushed back to Libya
item.description: The Armed Forces of Malta said it has no information on a boat carrying around 30 people that was intercepted and returned to Libya from Malta's search and rescue zone, in a reply to Newsbook questions that took two days to arrive. Alarm Phone said MRCC Rome identified RCC Malta as the responsible authority and that the group was pushed back to Libya on 24 October. The charity described the pushback as a violent violation and said it is pressing for answers.

item.title: Economists say Budget 2027 "pressed the panic button" on TCNs and tourists
item.description: Two leading economists said the government had "pressed the panic button" on non-EU workers and squeezed tourists to help fund costly election promises, reacting to Budget 2027. Philip von Brockdorff and Marisa Xuereb said the government needed to find new revenue for rising expenses, including a €1,000 super bonus pledge and continued blanket energy subsidies. Xuereb said the budget applied some "reverse logic" to the country's economic model.

item.title: Hungarian court orders Vatican Bank to pay €20m over Malta fund dispute
item.description: A Hungarian court has ordered the Vatican Bank to pay over €20 million in damages in a long-running dispute involving Malta-based investment fund Futura Investment Management, after the Institute for Works of Religion failed to submit a written defence in time. Futura says the bank reneged on legal commitments to fund the stalled sale of the historic Budapest Stock Exchange palace, and that the order reinforces its efforts to protect investors. The Vatican Bank downplayed the measure, saying it is an order in default rather than a judgment on the merits.
